name: wfct
title: Weighting function for nlsLM or nls weights=

origin.description: wfct can be supplied to the weights argument of nlsLM or nls, and facilitates specification of weighting schemes.

arguments.name: expr
arguments.text: An expression specifying the weighting scheme as described in the Details section below.

origin.details: The weighting function can take the predictor, the response, error from replicates, fitted values, and residuals. For fitted and resid, the model is fit unweighted, those values are extracted, and the expression is evaluated in an environment containing the data columns.
origin.value: The results of evaluation of expr in a new environment, yielding the vector of weights to be applied.
origin.example:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(minpack.lm))
Treated <- Puromycin[Puromycin$state == "treated", ]
nlsLM(rate ~ Vm * conc/(K + conc), data = Treated, start = c(Vm = 200, K = 0.05), weights = wfct(1/rate))

translation.description: wfct can be supplied to the weights argument of nls_lm or nlsLM, and facilitates specification of weighting schemes.

arguments.name: expr
arguments.text: A string expression for the weighting scheme, using column names, error, fitted, and resid as in the Details section.

translation.details: Pass the formula, data, and start map to Wfct.evaluate or wfct_eval. Expressions use ** for powers. When fitted or resid appear, an unweighted nlsLM fit is run with the same call. When error appears, replicate standard deviations are computed with sample variance and na.rm.
translation.value: A one-dimensional float array of weights.
translation.example:
from minpacklm.wfct import puromycin_treated, wfct_eval

Treated = puromycin_treated()
print(
    wfct_eval(
        "1/rate",
        formula="rate ~ Vm * conc/(K + conc)",
        data=Treated,
        start={"Vm": 200.0, "K": 0.05},
    )
)
